games.title: F-Zero
games.note: A Super Famicom launch game whose Mode 7 graphics scaled and rotated the track to fake 3D. Produced by Shigeru Miyamoto.

games.title: WipEout
games.note: Anti-gravity racing with a techno soundtrack and graphic design by The Designers Republic.

games.title: R.C. Pro-Am
games.note: Isometric radio-controlled car racing with missiles and bombs, four years before Super Mario Kart.

games.title: Micro Machines
games.note: Toy cars race across breakfast tables and pool tables; Andrew Graham's prototype California Buggy Boys was its base.

games.title: Rally Speedway
games.note: An early top-down racer for home computers with two-player racing.

games.title: Death Race
games.note: Considered the first 'scandalous' arcade game: drivers ran over stick-figure gremlins that turned into gravestones.

games.title: Carmageddon
games.note: Began as a banger-racing prototype; censored versions swapped pedestrians for zombies or robots.

games.title: Twisted Metal
games.note: Often called the first 'true' vehicular combat game. David Jaffe's pitch started out as 'Battle Cars'.

games.title: FlatOut
games.note: Drivers fly through the windscreen in big crashes, a feature reused for minigames like long jump.

games.title: Wreckfest
games.note: First shown as Next Car Game; early-access builds reached players from late 2013.

games.title: TrackMania
games.note: Built around a track editor; its free 2006 spin-off, TrackMania Nations, drew a large online community.

games.title: Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars
games.note: A PlayStation Network game where rocket-powered cars play football.

games.title: Rocket League
games.note: Free for PlayStation Plus members at launch in July 2015; it went free-to-play in 2020 after Epic bought Psyonix.

games.title: Excitebike
games.note: Its Design Mode let players build tracks, and in Japan save them on the Famicom Data Recorder tape drive.

games.title: Excite Truck
games.note: A Wii launch game steered by tilting the Wii Remote like a wheel.

games.title: Motocross Madness
games.note: Published by Microsoft; large outdoor areas let riders leave the track to chase big jumps.

games.title: MX vs. ATV Unleashed
games.note: Put motocross bikes and quad bikes on the same courses.

games.title: Wave Race 64
games.note: Jet ski racing on rolling waves that change how each lap handles.

games.title: SSX
games.note: Creative lead Steve Rechtschaffner invented boardercross, the snowboard race event that inspired the game.

games.title: Top Skater
games.note: Players balanced on a skateboard-shaped controller to race downhill and pull tricks.

games.title: Apocalypse
games.note: A shooter starring a digitized Bruce Willis; Neversoft reworked its engine for Tony Hawk's Pro Skater.
An early skateboarding game; dawdling players were chased by killer bees and the warning 'Skate or die!'.

games.title: Skate
games.note: Its 'Flick-it' controls read analog stick motions 120 times a second to turn them into tricks.

games.title: Session: Skate Sim
games.note: Each analog stick controls one of the skater's feet. Early access in 2019, full release in 2022.

links.took: Mode 7 racing; Shigeru Miyamoto first asked the team to make F-Zero for two players.
links.added: Split-screen racing for two, item boxes, a battle mode and Mario's cast.

src.t: Hideki Konno and Tadashi Sugiyama, Nintendo Classic Mini developer interview, 2017
Satoru Iwata and Hideki Konno, Iwata Asks: Mario Kart Wii, 2008

links.extra: Iwata later framed the goal as a two-player screen, which F-Zero's high speeds couldn't support.

links.took: Mario Kart's racing design, which Nick Burcombe played to trance music, sparking the idea.
links.added: Anti-gravity ships, weapon pads, a licensed techno soundtrack and The Designers Republic's graphics.

src.t: Nick Burcombe, GamesRadar+, 'How Super Mario Kart and dance music created WipEout'

links.extra: Burcombe played Super Mario Kart's 150cc races muted, with a trance track on his stereo.

links.took: Futuristic hover racing at very high speed on tracks above the ground.
links.added: Weapons, airbrakes and techno music, with a look aimed at club culture.

src.t: Wikipedia: F-Zero (lists Wipeout among games it inspired)
Nintendo Life, 2012, on Burcombe's Nintendo influence

links.extra: Often credited to F-Zero, but Nick Burcombe has said the Nintendo influence was Super Mario Kart, not F-Zero.

links.took: Anti-gravity racing with heavy, tilting ships and an electronic soundtrack.
links.added: Physics-based handling where both sticks pitch and strafe the craft through loops and drops.
links.extra: Wikipedia also names Rollcage and POD as inspirations.

links.took: F-Zero's extreme speed and boost-driven futuristic racing.
links.added: Twisting 3D tracks with loops and drops, raced in craft you pitch and strafe.

links.took: Named by Wikipedia among racing games F-Zero inspired; the source doesn't say which part.
links.added: Stock-car racing on Sega's texture-mapped Model 2 hardware, with linked cabinets.

links.took: Battle mode: Jaffe's team played 'a ton of Mario Kart in battle mode'.
links.added: Cars armed with machine guns and missiles in open arenas, and a dark cast of drivers.

src.t: David Jaffe, Twisted Metal oral history, MEL Magazine

links.took: Doom's deathmatch: the pitch was 'like Doom, but you're in cars'.
links.added: Armed vehicles hunting each other in arenas, including split-screen duels.

src.t: David Jaffe, Twisted Metal oral history, MEL Magazine

links.extra: The pitch was first called 'Battle Cars'.

links.took: A fighting-game roster: each driver has a story, a special weapon and an ending.
links.added: That character-select structure moved from fighters to killer cars.

src.t: David Jaffe, Twisted Metal oral history, MEL Magazine

links.extra: The oral history says its tone and characters drew on Mortal Kombat, then huge in arcades.

links.took: Death Race popularized the notorious idea of scoring points by running people down.
links.added: 3D cities and physics crashes; win by racing, wrecking every rival or hitting every pedestrian.
links.extra: Both drew on the 1975 film Death Race 2000, which Carmageddon was first licensed to adapt.

links.took: Destruction Derby popularized demolition racing built around smashing into rivals.
links.added: Ragdoll drivers thrown through windscreens, reused in minigames like long jump.

links.took: Bugbear's own FlatOut series: crash damage and banger racing.
links.added: Damage that changes how each car handles, plus lawnmowers, combines and other oddball vehicles.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls it a spiritual successor to FlatOut.

links.took: Destruction Derby's demolition events, which lead designer Janne Suur-Näkki named as an inspiration.
links.added: Detailed soft-body damage and online demolition derbies for up to 24 players.

src.t: Wikipedia: Wreckfest (cites IGN interview with Janne Suur-Näkki, 2014)

links.extra: The 1989 PC racer Street Rod is cited as another inspiration.

links.took: Stunt racing with loops and jumps, built around a track editor.
links.added: Instant restarts, online time leaderboards and a community trading home-made tracks.
links.extra: The retrospective calls Trackmania clearly influenced by Stunts; no statement from Nadeo was found.

links.took: Driving know-how from founder Dave Hagewood's vehicle mods for Unreal Tournament 2003.
links.added: Rocket-boosting, jumping cars that knock a giant ball into goals.
links.extra: Psyonix's vehicle mod became Unreal Tournament 2004's Onslaught mode.

links.took: Extreme-sports stunting, via Psyonix's earlier stunt-driving prototype Track Addict.
links.added: Cars doing aerial flips and boosts, aimed at a giant ball and goals.
links.extra: Track Addict drew partly on the Tony Hawk's and SSX series; adding a soccer ball turned it into Battle-Cars.

links.took: Big-air extreme-sports tricks, via Psyonix's stunt-driving prototype Track Addict.
links.added: Rocket cars flipping through the air to hit a giant ball.

links.took: Psyonix's own car-football game, which directly preceded and inspired Rocket League.
links.added: Polished physics, ranked online play, a free PlayStation Plus launch and later cross-platform matches.

links.took: Excitebike's side-scrolling engine, which Nintendo reused for Super Mario Bros.
links.added: A running, jumping hero exploring a scrolling world instead of racing a track.

links.took: Excitebike's name, big jumps and arcade off-road racing.
links.added: Motion steering with the Wii Remote and terrain that rises and falls during races.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls Excite Truck Excitebike's spiritual successor.

links.took: Excitebike popularized motocross racing built around jumps and landing angles.
links.added: Full 3D outdoor terrain, freestyle stunts and open areas to explore.

links.took: Rainbow Studios' off-road physics and big outdoor tracks.
links.added: Quad bikes, trucks and other vehicles racing motocross bikes on the same courses.

links.took: Rare's own R.C. Pro-Am; the project was once called 'RC Pro-Am 64'.
links.added: Karts, hovercraft and planes, an adventure hub island and boss races.

src.t: Wikipedia: Diddy Kong Racing (cites Kevin Bayliss and Lee Schuneman)

links.extra: The project also passed through time-travel strategy and 'Adventure Racers' phases.

links.took: Kart racing with items; Lee Musgrave said the aim was to run as fast as Mario Kart 64.
links.added: An adventure mode with a hub island and boss races, plus hovercraft and planes.

src.t: Lee Musgrave (Rare), quoted in Wikipedia: Diddy Kong Racing

links.took: Elements of Wave Race 64, per GamePro, such as racing across water.
links.added: Hovercraft as one of three vehicles, swapped with karts and planes between courses.
links.extra: GamePro said it combines elements of Mario Kart 64, Wave Race 64 and Pilotwings 64.

links.took: Mario Kart's item-based kart racing and battle arenas.
links.added: A powerslide turbo system, an adventure mode and Crash Bandicoot's characters.
links.extra: Jason Rubin pushed the turbo system to make it more involving than older kart racers.

links.took: An adventure mode with a hub world and boss races, as in Diddy Kong Racing.
links.added: Crash's world, with his villains as bosses and skill-based powerslide boosts.
links.extra: Wikipedia says it drew heavy inspiration from Mario Kart and Diddy Kong Racing.

links.took: Super Sprint popularized fast top-down multiplayer racing with tiny cars.
links.added: Toy-scale cars on household tracks like tables and bathtubs, with a scrolling camera.

links.took: Its two-player racing, which Wikipedia says Micro Machines' two-player mode drew on.
links.added: Head-to-head races where a player scores by leaving the other behind off-screen.
links.extra: Galoob, owner of the Micro Machines toys, asked Codemasters to make the game.

links.took: Super Sprint popularized top-down track racing with car upgrades between races.
links.added: An isometric view, radio-controlled cars, and missiles and bombs to fire at rivals.

links.took: Downhill skating levels: Neversoft prototyped long downhill runs after playing Top Skater across the street.
links.added: Open skateparks with goals, trick combos, real pro skaters and a punk soundtrack.

src.t: Mick West and David Stohl (Neversoft), The Ringer oral history, 2019

links.extra: The arcade machine was in a bowling alley across the street from Neversoft.

links.took: Neversoft's Apocalypse engine; the first prototype even put Bruce Willis's character on a skateboard.
links.added: Skateboarding with real pros, trick combos and score goals.

src.t: GamesRadar+, Tony Hawk's Pro Skater making-of, 2019

links.took: 720° popularized skateboarding in games, with ramps, tricks and scoring.
links.added: Real pro skaters, combo-driven trick scoring and timed goals in open levels.

links.took: Tony Hawk's Pro Skater popularized skateboarding games with real pros and open levels.
links.added: 'Flick-it' analog stick controls and grounded physics in an open city.

links.took: Skate's grounded, analog-stick skateboarding; Wikipedia calls Session its spiritual successor.
links.added: Strict board physics with each stick controlling one foot, and a replay editor for filming.
